chapter: Other bands: Royal Jazz, H&J, Rainbow Room
title: The Original Royal Jazz Band under Joe Harris
summary: Before Celestin he played with Joe Harris's Original Royal Jazz Band, which played Odd Fellows parades and fairground picnics and weddings four or five nights a week.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Was there any other band you played with for a while before you joined Celestan, aside from just jobbing around, you know?

Well, yeah, years ago I used to play with a band called Original Royal Jazz Band. A fella called Joe Harris, he's a trombone player. He died probably a few years ago. He was the leader of this band. And he belonged to the Oddfellas. That's how I happened to play at the fairgrounds so often. And then we used to play parades too. He'd get up a band and we'd play a parade for the Oddfellas. And he was one of the big shots in the Oddfellas. So he would get all these jobs, you see? Yeah. And we'd parade them all over town. And then that Monday night they'd have a picnic, a dance that Monday night at the fairground. And we would play, we'd be the small band. We would just use about six, seven pieces. And then I can't remember who it was now. He used to have the big band. Well, let me see. Yeah, Papa Celestine. Yes, Papa Celestine used to have the big band. That's how I happened to see when he used to knock on that red with that tuba foot to start the band off. Yeah, well, we'd be about half a block from them playing with the small band and Papa would be over with his large band playing for his dance. And then a lot of times there used to be picnics out there during the day. Well, this Joe Harris would get these jobs too, you see. So I played quite a few jobs with him. He used to live on Maganoya Street years ago. And he was a wonderful fellow. And we all had, really got along all right.
Remember any other people in the band, the trumpet player, Cornette, who used to?

Well, yes, Harry Vanette was playing trumpet. Harry Vanette. He was playing trumpet with this band. And you see, a boy played banjo called Jack, Lil Jack. Gee, I don't know if he's away or what. I haven't seen him for years. But Harry Vanette, he's from St. Rose, Louisiana. He played with the band a good while. Well, until the band broke up, then we all went different ways, you see. We all played, got to playing with different bands after that. But scattered. But so I haven't seen none of these boys, or Joe Harris died, you see. I haven't seen none of these other boys for quite a while.
What did you have in the band? About the same as what you're playing with now? The same number of instruments? Same kind of instruments?
Yes, I believe we had all but a piano. Oh, yeah. Yeah.

Trombone, clarinet, trumpet, banjo, bass, violin. No, it's a fellow, he been dead for years too. Frank Mills, he was the bass player. You heard of him. Yeah, he was a real good bass player too. He played with this band too. And sometimes he would take sicken, so we would use chestisardis. Oh, yeah? Yeah, chestisardis. He was a player with this Joe Harris sometimes. And so we had a pretty good band then too. We were playing about four or five nights a week.

Yeah, playing weddings and different parties and balls, you know. Mm-hmm. And so we were going over pretty big. Well, that was, I believe it was after, you know, I quit playing with this boy, Gerald Kendrick. And I got with this, Gerald, the original Royal Jazz Band. So we went around quite a few times.
